reason:
Measured the specific new claim on state=print and it is arithmetically true but evidentially empty, and both halves of the proposed fix are disqualifying.

(1) THE 90px CLAIM IS TRUE AND IS NOT NEW. approach/print at 1440: struck .b-behindTitle "City hotel shortlist" top 706, .b-behindState "Not going ahead" 728-744, .b-behindNote "One of them did not happen." 764-786 - an 80px span in the 220px past column. Identical on record/print. But the same three co-occur TIGHTER on record/desk (1335-1400, 65px), which is a surface round 7 drove and refuted, and round 7 already granted the adjacency in terms ("the row chip it sits under is a status token that cannot follow it without changing MILESTONE_STATE_LABELS product-wide"). The seat has re-measured a co-occurrence the prior refutation conceded, on a surface that is not even the tightest case, and offered it as the new evidence. It does not meet the stated objection.

(2) "THREE WAYS" DOUBLE-COUNTS THE REMEDY. The strikethrough is not a statement - that is the whole premise of the paid-for fix recorded at render-b.js:342-345 and b.css:889-891 ("a line drawn through 15px text at 28% is not a statement. The row says what it is, in words, so the accessible name carries it too"). The mono chip exists BECAUSE the line alone does not say it. Counting the mark and the words that exist to compensate for the mark as two independent registers inflates two into three. What is actually on paper is two text forms doing two different jobs in two deliberate registers: an 11px Geist Mono row status token at 62% ink (F.stateLabel.cancelled, the product-global MILESTONE_STATE_LABELS at fixture.js:70-76) and a 15px Geist sentence that partitions the head total "3 moments".

(3) THE PRIMARY FIX MAKES THE MEASURED PROBLEM WORSE. "One moment is not going ahead." would set the identical five-word phrase 20px below a chip already reading "Not going ahead" (chip bottom 744, note top 764). Verbatim repetition of a phrase inside 40px on a 220px column is a harder defect than two phrasings of one fact - the current sentence at least does a different job (it partitions a total) rather than echoing the row above it word for word. The seat proposes to convert a register difference into a literal duplication and calls it one vocabulary.

(4) THE COUNT HALF REINSTATES A ROUND-6 DEFECT AND BREAKS A PASSING GATE. The proposed plural branch is dropped.length + " moments are not going ahead." That puts noun-plus-number back beside the head "3 moments" - exactly what render-b.js:395-399 records as fixed ("The head carries the only total - it counts the rows a reader can see. This line partitions that total; it never recounts it, because the same noun printing two different numbers on one sheet is the whole defect"). interaction-check.mjs:1988-2005 asserts, for approach/print and record/desk, that no visible note matches [0-9]+ followed by " moments". The proposed string fails that assertion by construction. A fix that red-lights a currently green gate assertion is not an improvement at any bar.

(5) THE SECOND HALF REGRESSES THE WEDDING MORNING. "Give all four surfaces the guest shape" means the dayOf branch gains the dropped clause. Verified by driving state=day: the [data-when="open"] node renders there (dropped is non-empty on the day clock, by the deliberate rule at render-b.js:316-320 that cancelled moments stay in the record on BOTH clocks), so the guest shape would close the morning block with "The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead." That is precisely the regression render-b.js:404-406 records as fixed ("on the wedding morning the last thing a guest read before the footer was a cancelled hotel search"), and the morning closing sentence is on round 9 settled list. It would also delete the owner only statement of how many of the three actually happened, which the head total does not give.

(6) THE RESIDUE IS ROUND 7 RESIDUE. A present-tense status token above a past-tense sentence, under a heading that reads "Behind you", is a tense choice inside an explicitly past frame - weighed once and called defensible. "Thing" and "them" avoid the noun "moment" for the documented reason in (4), so the third-noun complaint is aimed at the remedy as well.

One genuinely useful by-product of this measurement is recorded in the sharpened fix: it retires round 7 own suggested reword.
sharpenedFix: Change nothing here. Two specific do-nots, both established by this round measurement: (a) Do NOT take round 7 sharpened fix ("One of them did not happen." -> "One of them is not going ahead."). That verdict never measured the printed sheet; at 20px below the row chip it would print "Not going ahead" and "is not going ahead" as near-identical strings inside 40px on a 220px column - worse than the tense mismatch it was meant to cure. (b) Do NOT introduce the noun "moments" with a number into either dropped-note branch - it fails the "nothing recounts it in the same words" assertion on approach/print and record/desk. If a future round still wants the printed block tightened, the only candidate worth measuring is the opposite of this finding: on surfaces where every row is listed and the cancelled row already carries its own chip, the partition SENTENCE is the redundant element, not the vocabulary. That is a deletion, and it is currently blocked by "the past is stated once" (exactly one visible note at three call sites) and by the rule that the block must close on a sentence rather than a cancelled row - so it needs those two decisions reopened, not a copy edit.
